what: VC2 §六 -- the one P0 this round changes, decided from matched-content evidence and written BEFORE any product code was touched.

evidenceBasis.matchedContent: qa-v5/visual-convergence/matched-content-contract.json -- MATCHED-CONTENT HARNESS PROVEN. Same H.264 elementary stream, per-pixel-verified decode, same injected copy hash, same viewport/DPR/pointer class/card box/cover fit on both pages.

candidates.system: A. Dynamic Grid / Motion / Camera Dolly
candidates.userFeedback: 卡片运动时的间距与轨迹
whatTheMatchedEvidenceSays: Spacing is NOT the problem. At rest, at every viewport, the two pages agree exactly: horizontal gutter 17.337 px and vertical gutter 16.616 px at 1440x900, identical card centres, identical projected sizes, identical row stagger. Under a slow drag, a pointer sweep, a mobile touch drag and a long wrapping touch drag, every gated observable is inside its pre-registered threshold -- gutters to 1.8 px p95 or better, stagger to 0.06 px on a slow drag.

Two real divergences exist, and neither is a spacing error. (1) FAST FLICK: our fling carries 2.0% further -- total travel 832.1 px against the Target's 815.6 px on the same dispatched input -- so the page settles 16.6 px past the Target's landing point, and the cards there project 6.03 px (1.5%) smaller. Mid-flight centre p95 24.7 px against a 7.2 px threshold; projected width p95 7.09 px against 2.05 px. The dolly ENVELOPE matches (excursion 0.5789 vs 0.5761); it is the fling distance that differs, and the size difference follows from where the grid stops. (2) ORIENTATION CHANGE: our relayout completes about 330 ms earlier than the Target's. Both pages start and end at the same row phase (126.42 -> -139.6 on both); in between the Target sweeps for ~1 s and we arrive early, with one 36.7 px single-frame step where the Target's largest is 3.9 px.
candidates.whyNot: Both findings are real, both are now measured rather than assumed, and neither clears §六's visibility bar. The flick difference is a landing-point difference on an infinite grid: a viewer looking at one page sees a flick that feels right, and only a synchronised side-by-side shows the 16.6 px phase. The orientation finding lives inside a 700 ms transient. Fixing either would move a number, and §一.10 rules out a round whose only result is that a number moved. Both are carried forward as the ranked motion candidates for the next round -- which is the answer §一.6 asked for: 'no motion P0' is replaced by two named, measured, reproducible ones.

whatTheMatchedEvidenceSays: This is the first round where the glass can be judged at all: until now the two pages were showing different clips. On matched media the page-wide luma difference outside the footer band is +2.0 to +3.9 (candidate brighter) at the four viewports -- real, but small, and the same signature Sprint 1 already attributed to the output transform.

Sprint 1's code-to-code audit found the card program transcription-complete: every constant matches the shipped bundle, the tint/rim foldings are inert, the served HDR is byte-identical. No un-audited optical subsystem has been named.
candidates.whyNot: §一.2 closes exposure, tone mapping and page brightness for this round, and §一.10 rules out another SUBTLE-BUT-PAGE-WIDE glass result. With the card program proven complete and no new root cause identified, picking B would mean tuning a constant and hoping -- exactly the failure mode the brief forbids. The matched-content harness built this round is what a future glass round needs, and it now exists.

candidates.system: C. Typography / Footer / Brand -- the page chrome band
candidates.userFeedback: 字体与 Footer 完整视觉
whatTheMatchedEvidenceSays: THE TARGET PAINTS A 144 px GRADIENT SCRIM ACROSS THE FULL WIDTH OF EVERY PAGE. Its own DOM: div.absolute.inset-x-0.bottom-0.h-36, background linear-gradient(to top, black/60, transparent), inside the fixed footer container at z-20 -- so it darkens the cards and their labels, not just the background. Our page has no such element at any viewport (recon.json scrims: target 1, local 0).

Measured on matched full-page stills, mean luma of the bottom 144 rows, target vs candidate: 1440x900 39.08 vs 52.26 (+13.19), 390x844 37.50 vs 54.55 (+17.05), 844x390 28.82 vs 43.32 (+14.49), 700x700 33.28 vs 52.19 (+18.91). Isolating the scrim from the page-wide difference (bottom-144 delta minus the delta of the 144 rows above it) leaves +11.18, +13.15, +11.02 and +16.80. At the very last screen row the difference is +18.9, +16.3, +25.0 and +43.2 luma levels.

The footer's own geometry differs too. On mobile (390x844) the Target keeps the caption/wordmark and the CTA in ONE row and stacks only inside the wordmark link (flex-col below lg); ours stacks the whole footer, which puts the brand block at y=750.8 where the Target's wordmark sits at y=809.6 -- 59 px too high -- and makes the footer 99.1 px tall against the Target's 61.2 px.

The brand: the Target renders its wordmark as artwork in a box of width min(26vw, 148px) with drop-shadow(0 2px 12px rgba(0,0,0,0.45)) -- 148x19.8 px on desktop, 101x13.6 px on the phone. Ours is a 28x14 px mark plus 20 px type, 132.3x20 px on desktop and the same 132.3x20 px on the phone: it does not scale with the viewport at all.
The CTA pill matches except for one element -- the Target's pill carries a top-half sheen (linear-gradient(white/24, transparent), opacity .7) that ours does not have.

chosenP0.title: The page chrome band: the missing bottom scrim, the footer's viewport law, and the brand box

sixQualification.matchedEvidenceRepeatable: yes -- measured on §三-proven matched media and matched copy, at four viewports, and the structural read is reproducible from vc2-recon.mjs
sixQualification.differenceVisibleToTheEye: yes -- the bottom 144 rows of every viewport, up to 43 luma levels at the last row; the bottom sixth of the page is a different colour
sixQualification.notCausedByMedia: yes -- identical decoded frames on both pages (five of six categories bit-identical)
sixQualification.notCausedByCopyLength: yes -- identical injected strings, identical copy hash; the scrim carries no text at all
sixQualification.notAOneToThreeGreyMicroDifference: yes -- 11 to 17 luma levels of scrim-specific ramp, 19 to 43 at the last row
sixQualification.visibleAt1xAfterFix: yes -- adding the scrim changes the bottom sixth of every full frame; the mobile footer moves 59 px
sixQualification.clearCodeRootCause: yes -- src/ui/PageOverlay.ts emits no scrim element, and src/style.css stacks the whole footer below 720px instead of stacking only the wordmark link below 1024px
sixQualification.oneSystemOnly: yes -- page chrome presentation: PageOverlay markup and its stylesheet block. No layout, no motion, no glass, no card typography.

forbiddenThisRound: SourceExact layout contract, plane size, cell pitch, sphere radius
card label markup and card typography CSS (TileLabelLayer is left untouched: the card typography contract already passes and must keep passing)
expectedVisibleResult: The bottom 144 px of every viewport gains a gradient to 60% black, grounding the footer and pulling the bottom row of cards down in tone -- the bottom-144 mean luma should fall by roughly the measured 11-17 level ramp at all four viewports.

On the phone the footer becomes one row again: the caption and wordmark stack inside their own link at the bottom-left, the CTA stays bottom-right, and the brand block lands where the Target's does instead of 59 px above it.
The wordmark scales with the viewport (min(26vw, 148px)) and carries the same drop shadow, so the footer band reads at the same weight on a phone as on a desktop.
The CTA pill gains its top sheen.
chosenP0.brandHonesty: The Target's wordmark is its own studio logo and is never copied into this repo. What is matched is the PRESENTATION -- the box, the scaling law, the drop shadow -- rendered with our own ATELIER mark as inline SVG so it scales inside that box.
